fr: dossiers administratifs des salariés / données du personnel
def: The administrative information an employer holds on each member of staff, from contract and identity details to pay and absence history.

formal.ex: The Company shall maintain accurate [[employee records]] and update them promptly following any change in an employee's circumstances.

everyday.ex: Can you check the [[staff records]]? I think her address is out of date.
everyday.ex_us: Can you check the [[employee files]]? I think her address is out of date.

collocations: to keep employee records up to date
note_fr: « Records » est le terme générique pour les données et documents tenus sur les salariés ; « personnel file » désigne plutôt le dossier individuel. Ne dites pas « administrative files of the employees ».

def: The forms, documents and administrative steps needed to complete a process.

formal.ex: All [[administrative formalities]] relating to the hire must be completed before the employee's first day.

everyday.ex: The [[paperwork]] for a new starter in France takes longer than head office expects.
everyday.ex_us: The [[paperwork]] for a new hire in France takes longer than headquarters expects.

informal.ex: Our CFO is convinced that French payroll is ninety per cent [[red tape]].
informal.ex_us: Our CFO is convinced that French payroll is ninety percent [[red tape]].

note_fr: « Paperwork » est indénombrable : jamais « paperworks ». « Red tape » est péjoratif (lourdeur bureaucratique) : à éviter devant l'administration elle-même.

def: Documents provided as evidence to back up a declaration, a payment or an entry in a file.

formal.ex: Any change of bank details must be accompanied by the relevant [[supporting documentation]].

everyday.ex: We'll need [[proof]] of address before we can update his file.

note_fr: « Justificative pieces » n'existe pas. « Documentation » est indénombrable (pas de « documentations »). Pour un justificatif de dépense, on dit « receipt ».

def: The part of an HR system in which employees view their payslips and update some of their own data - address, bank details, leave requests - themselves.

formal.ex: Payslips are made available in electronic form on the [[employee self-service portal]], unless the employee objects.

everyday.ex: Just update your address on [[the HR portal]] - you don't need to email us.

note_fr: Souvent abrégé « ESS ». En France, le salarié peut refuser le bulletin de paie électronique : prévoyez toujours une solution papier.

def: The task of typing or loading information into a computer system.

formal.ex: Payroll [[data entry]] shall be carried out exclusively by authorised members of the HR team.
formal.ex_us: Payroll [[data entry]] shall be performed exclusively by authorized members of the HR team.

everyday.ex: Could you [[key in]] the new starters before Thursday?
everyday.ex_us: Could you [[enter]] the new hires before Thursday?

collocations: to key data into the system
note_fr: « Saisir » ne se traduit ni par « to seize » (saisir un bien) ni par « to grasp ». À l'écrit : « to enter » ; à l'oral britannique : « to key in » ou « to input ».

def: A mistake made when typing information into a system, such as a wrong figure or a misplaced decimal point.

formal.ex: The overpayment resulted from an [[input error]] in the October payroll.

everyday.ex: It wasn't the system - it was a simple [[keying error]], two zeros instead of one.
everyday.ex_us: It wasn't the system - it was a simple [[typo]], two zeros instead of one.

informal.ex: Someone made a [[fat-finger error]] and paid him ten times his bonus.

note_fr: « Fat-finger error » est familier mais très courant en finance pour une faute de frappe coûteuse. « Typo » s'emploie pour un texte comme pour un chiffre.

def: A box in a form or a system that must be filled in before the record can be saved.

formal.ex: All [[mandatory fields]] must be completed before the record is submitted to payroll.
formal.ex_us: All [[required fields]] must be completed before the record is submitted to payroll.

everyday.ex: The system won't let you save it if a [[mandatory field]] is blank.
everyday.ex_us: The system won't let you save it if a [[required field]] is blank.

collocations: to fill in a field (UK) / to fill out a field (US)
note_fr: « Obligatory » existe mais sonne vieilli : préférez « mandatory » (UK) ou « required » (US). Remplir un formulaire : « to fill in » (UK), « to fill out » (US).

fr: sortir un état / lancer une extraction
def: To generate a list or summary of data from a system.

formal.ex: The HRIS can [[generate a report]] of all employees whose medical check-up is overdue.

everyday.ex: I'll [[run a report]] on everyone who joined last quarter and send it over.

informal.ex: Give me ten minutes and I'll [[pull the data]] for you.

note_fr: Un état (document) n'est pas un « state » : dites « report » ou « listing ». « Extraction » se dit « extract » (nom) ; « to extract data » existe mais « to pull » ou « to run a report » sont plus naturels.

def: The employees who join and leave the company during a given period, which HR and payroll must process.

formal.ex: A monthly list of [[joiners and leavers]] shall be sent to the payroll provider by the fifth working day.
formal.ex_us: A monthly list of [[new hires and separations]] shall be sent to the payroll vendor by the fifth business day.

everyday.ex: We had twelve [[starters and leavers]] in March, so payroll took a bit longer.
everyday.ex_us: We had twelve [[new hires and terminations]] in March, so payroll took a little longer.

note_fr: Ne traduisez pas « entrées / sorties » par « entries / exits ». Dans le vocabulaire américain de la paie, « termination » couvre tout départ, démission comprise (« voluntary termination »).

def: The date on which a person's employment ends and after which they are removed from the payroll.

formal.ex: The [[termination date]] shall be the last day of the notice period, whether or not the notice is worked.

everyday.ex: What's his [[leaving date]]? Payroll needs it for the final payslip.
everyday.ex_us: What's his [[last day]]? Payroll needs it for the final paycheck.

collocations: to bring forward a leaving date
the last day in the office
note_fr: La date de sortie correspond à la fin du contrat (fin du préavis, même non effectué), pas forcément au dernier jour de présence : précisez « last day in the office » pour le dernier jour travaillé.

def: The registers an employer must keep by law and make available to the authorities, such as the single staff register.

formal.ex: All [[statutory registers]] shall be kept at each establishment and made available to the labour inspector on request.
formal.ex_us: All [[legally required records]] shall be kept at each establishment and made available to the inspector upon request.

everyday.ex: Before the inspection, let's make sure the [[mandatory registers]] are all up to date.
everyday.ex_us: Before the inspection, let's make sure the [[required records]] are all up to date.

collocations: to make an entry in a register
note_fr: En France, plusieurs registres sont exigés (registre unique du personnel, registres liés à la sécurité...). Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, on parle surtout de « records » à conserver plutôt que de registres au sens formel.

def: Information that an employer must by law display or otherwise make available to staff, such as the labour inspector's contact details or working hours.

formal.ex: The employer shall ensure that all [[statutory notices]] are displayed in a place accessible to staff.
formal.ex_us: The employer shall ensure that all [[mandatory postings]] are displayed in a location accessible to employees.

everyday.ex: Is anyone looking after the [[mandatory notices]] at the new site?
everyday.ex_us: Is anyone looking after the [[labor law posters]] at the new site?

collocations: to keep notices up to date
note_fr: Les États-Unis ont aussi des obligations d'affichage, fédérales et propres à chaque État (« labor law posters ») ; le Royaume-Uni beaucoup moins. En France, certaines informations peuvent désormais être communiquées « par tout moyen » (intranet, par exemple).

fr: données de référence des salariés (données maîtres)
def: The core, relatively stable information about each employee - identity, contract, position, bank details - on which every HR and payroll process depends.

formal.ex: Any change to [[employee master data]] shall be validated by a second member of the team before payroll is run.

everyday.ex: If the [[core employee data]] is wrong, every report you run is wrong too.

note_fr: « Data » s'emploie le plus souvent au singulier en anglais des affaires (« the data is wrong ») ; le pluriel « the data are » relève du registre scientifique.

def: A mandatory written document in larger French companies setting out health and safety rules, the general rules on discipline and the range of sanctions.

formal.ex: Any amendment to the [[internal regulations]] must be submitted to the works council and filed with the relevant authorities before it takes effect.

everyday.ex: You can't add a new sanction just by email - it has to go into the [[company rules]] first.
everyday.ex_us: You can't add a new sanction just by email - it has to go into the [[work rules]] first.

collocations: to consult the works council on the internal regulations
to be set out in the internal regulations
note_fr: Rien à voir avec un « staff handbook » facultatif : le règlement intérieur est obligatoire à partir de 50 salariés, son contenu est encadré par la loi et il doit suivre une procédure (consultation du CSE, dépôt, communication à l'inspection du travail).

explain.written: The règlement intérieur is a document that French companies with 50 or more employees must adopt, setting out health and safety rules and the disciplinary rules and sanctions; it only takes effect after the works council has been consulted and the document has been filed and sent to the labour inspectorate.
explain.spoken: It's a sort of official rulebook that's compulsory once you reach fifty staff. It covers safety and discipline, and you can't change it without consulting the works council and filing it.

def: A document that describes, step by step, how recurring tasks must be carried out and by whom.

formal.ex: The payroll [[procedures manual]] shall be reviewed annually and approved by the HR Director.

everyday.ex: It's all in [[the procedures]] - who checks what, and when.
everyday.ex_us: It's all in [[the playbook]] - who checks what, and when.

note_fr: « Policy » (politique : ce que l'on fait et pourquoi) ≠ « procedure » (procédure : comment on le fait). « Process » désigne l'enchaînement global des étapes.

def: A detailed, task-level description of exactly how to perform one operation, often with screenshots.

formal.ex: Each payroll control is described in a [[work instruction]] stating the source data, the check performed and the evidence retained.
formal.ex_us: Each payroll control is described in a [[standard operating procedure]] stating the source data, the check performed and the evidence retained.

everyday.ex: There's a [[how-to guide]] for the bank file, so anyone can cover for Julie.
everyday.ex_us: There's an [[SOP]] for the bank file, so anyone can cover for Julie.

collocations: to write up a work instruction
note_fr: « Operating mode » est un calque : il n'est pas compris dans ce sens. « SOP » se prononce lettre par lettre (/ˌes oʊ ˈpiː/).

fr: adaptation locale / exception pays (à une politique groupe)
def: A part of a group policy that is adapted or excluded in one country because local law or practice requires it.

formal.ex: Where local law imposes stricter requirements, a [[local exception]] shall be documented and approved by Group HR.
formal.ex_us: Where local law imposes stricter requirements, a [[country-specific exception]] shall be documented and approved by Corporate HR.

everyday.ex: We'll need a [[local carve-out]] for France - the template's disciplinary section simply doesn't work here.
everyday.ex_us: We'll need a [[country carve-out]] for France - the template's disciplinary section simply doesn't work here.

collocations: to carve out France from a policy
to localise a policy (UK) / to localize a policy (US)
note_fr: « Carve-out » (découpe) s'emploie aussi en M&A (détourage d'une activité) : le contexte lève l'ambiguïté. Le verbe : « to carve something out of the policy ».

fr: contrevenir à / être contraire à (la loi)
def: To break a law or rule, often without intending to, and get into trouble as a result.

formal.ex: As drafted, the clause would [[contravene]] French rules on the processing of sickness absence.
formal.ex_us: As drafted, the clause would [[violate]] French rules on the processing of sickness absence.

everyday.ex: If we roll out that template as it is, we'll [[fall foul of]] French law within a week.
everyday.ex_us: If we roll out that template as is, we'll [[run afoul of]] French law within a week.

collocations: to fall foul of the rules
to fall foul of the regulator
to stay on the right side of the law
note_fr: « To fall foul of » est britannique ; l'américain dit « to run afoul of ». « To violate » est neutre en américain mais paraît fort en anglais britannique, où l'on préfère « to breach » ou « to contravene ».

fr: primauté du droit local (sur la politique groupe)
def: The principle that, where a group policy conflicts with mandatory local rules, the local rules apply.

formal.ex: In the event of any conflict between this Policy and mandatory local legislation, the latter shall [[take precedence]].

everyday.ex: Whatever the global policy says, French law [[overrides]] it on this point.

informal.ex: I know it's a group standard, but the Labour Code [[trumps]] it, I'm afraid.
informal.ex_us: I know it's a corporate standard, but the Labor Code [[trumps]] it, I'm afraid.

note_fr: « Primacy » est un terme de droit constitutionnel ou européen ; dans une politique RH, on écrit « shall take precedence » ou « shall prevail ». Précisez « mandatory » : seules les règles impératives l'emportent.

fr: tableau des durées de conservation (des documents RH)
def: A table listing each category of document, how long it must be kept, in what form, and when it must be destroyed.

formal.ex: Payroll records shall be retained in accordance with the [[document retention schedule]] annexed to this policy.
formal.ex_us: Payroll records shall be retained in accordance with the [[records retention schedule]] attached to this policy.

everyday.ex: Before we shred anything, can we check the [[retention schedule]]?

note_fr: Attention à la prononciation de « schedule » : /ˈʃedjuːl/ au Royaume-Uni, /ˈskedʒuːl/ aux États-Unis. Les durées diffèrent selon les pays et les documents : ne transposez jamais un tableau groupe sans vérification locale.

def: A signature made by hand in ink on paper, as opposed to an electronic signature.

formal.ex: Where a [[handwritten signature]] is required, the original document shall be returned by post.
formal.ex_us: Where a [[handwritten signature]] is required, the original document shall be returned by mail.

everyday.ex: Does the bank really need a [[wet-ink signature]], or will DocuSign do?
everyday.ex_us: Does the bank really need a [[wet signature]], or will DocuSign do?

note_fr: « Manuscript signature » n'existe pas : « manuscript » désigne un manuscrit. Dites « handwritten » ou, dans le jargon, « wet-ink ».

def: The weight a document carries as proof, for instance in an audit or before a court.

formal.ex: Digitised payslips stored in a certified vault retain their full [[evidential value]].
formal.ex_us: Digitized pay statements stored in a certified vault retain their full [[evidentiary value]].

everyday.ex: A scan on someone's laptop won't [[stand up as evidence]] if URSSAF questions it.
everyday.ex_us: A scan on someone's laptop won't [[hold up as evidence]] if URSSAF questions it.

note_fr: « Probative value » existe mais reste très technique (plutôt américain). Le britannique dit « evidential », l'américain « evidentiary ». « Proof value » n'existe pas.

def: A written act by which a company head transfers part of his or her powers - and, under French law, the related criminal liability - to a manager.

formal.ex: The site director holds a [[delegation of authority]] in matters of health and safety and working time.

everyday.ex: He can sign the warning himself - he's got [[delegated authority]] for HR matters.

collocations: to grant a delegation of authority
to accept a delegation in writing
note_fr: Dans un groupe anglo-saxon, « delegation of authority » désigne surtout une matrice de seuils de signature. En droit français, une délégation valable (compétence, autorité, moyens) transfère aussi la responsabilité pénale : précisez-le, ce n'est pas intuitif pour vos interlocuteurs.

explain.written: Under French law, a valid délégation de pouvoirs - granted to a manager with the necessary competence, authority and resources - transfers not only decision-making power but also the criminal liability attached to it.
explain.spoken: In France a delegation isn't just about who can sign. If it's done properly, the manager who holds it also takes on the legal risk - including criminal liability - in that area.

def: The further transfer of delegated powers by the person who holds them to someone lower down the organisation.

formal.ex: Any [[sub-delegation]] shall be made in writing and shall meet the same conditions of competence, authority and means as the original delegation.
formal.ex_us: Any [[subdelegation]] shall be made in writing and shall meet the same conditions of competence, authority and means as the original delegation.

everyday.ex: The plant manager can [[pass on]] his safety authority to the shift supervisors, but only in writing.
everyday.ex_us: The plant manager can [[pass down]] his safety authority to the shift supervisors, but only in writing.

note_fr: « Delegate » se prononce différemment selon la nature du mot : nom /ˈdelɪɡət/, verbe /ˈdelɪɡeɪt/. La subdélégation suppose que le subdélégataire dispose lui aussi de la compétence, de l'autorité et des moyens nécessaires.

def: The exposure of a company officer to criminal prosecution in his or her own name for offences committed in running the business.

formal.ex: Breaches of the rules on undeclared work may give rise to [[personal criminal liability]] for the company's legal representative.

everyday.uk: to be personally on the hook
everyday.us: to be personally on the hook
everyday.ex: If there's no valid delegation, it's the managing director who's [[personally on the hook]].
everyday.ex_us: If there's no valid delegation, it's the general manager who's [[personally on the hook]].

note_fr: « Penal responsibility » est un calque. En anglais, « liability » = responsabilité juridique ; « responsibility » = responsabilité au sens de mission. Le droit français engage facilement la responsabilité pénale du dirigeant en droit du travail, ce qui surprend souvent les groupes étrangers.

fr: pouvoir de signature / habilitation à signer
def: The right, given to a named person, to sign certain documents or approve certain payments on the company's behalf.

formal.ex: Only an [[authorised signatory]] may sign employment contracts on behalf of the Company.
formal.ex_us: Only an [[authorized signatory]] may sign employment contracts on behalf of the Company.

everyday.ex: I don't have [[signing authority]] above fifty thousand euros, so it'll need the CFO.
everyday.ex_us: I don't have [[signature authority]] above fifty thousand euros, so it'll need the CFO.

collocations: to sign on behalf of the company
note_fr: « Signature power » est peu idiomatique. « To be empowered to sign » est correct mais très formel ; à l'oral, « I can't sign that off » suffit.

fr: attestation d'emploi (pour un salarié en poste)
def: A short letter from the employer confirming that a person works for the company, usually stating position, start date and sometimes salary.

formal.ex: Please find enclosed a [[confirmation of employment]] for submission to your landlord.
formal.ex_us: Please find enclosed a [[verification of employment]] for submission to your landlord.

everyday.ex: Could HR do me an [[employment letter]] for the flat I'm trying to rent?
everyday.ex_us: Could HR give me an [[employment verification letter]] for the apartment I'm trying to rent?

collocations: to issue a letter confirming employment
to request a letter from HR
note_fr: Ne confondez pas avec le certificat de travail remis en fin de contrat. « Attestation » est rare en anglais courant : préférez « letter confirming... » ou « certificate ».

fr: attestation de salaire (pour le calcul des indemnités journalières)
def: A statement of an employee's recent earnings that the French employer provides to the health insurance fund so that it can calculate daily sickness, maternity or work-injury benefits.

formal.ex: The [[salary certificate]] is now generated from the monthly social declaration once a sick-leave event has been reported.
formal.ex_us: The [[wage statement]] is now generated from the monthly social declaration once a sick-leave event has been reported.

everyday.ex: The fund hasn't paid her yet because it never received the [[earnings statement]].

collocations: to report a period of sick leave
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur verse lui-même le « Statutory Sick Pay » ; aux États-Unis, il n'existe pas de régime fédéral d'indemnisation de la maladie de courte durée. Le mécanisme français (caisse + complément employeur) doit donc être expliqué.

explain.written: The attestation de salaire is the statement of recent earnings that a French employer sends to the health insurance fund, now mostly through the monthly social declaration, so that the fund can calculate the employee's daily sickness, maternity or work-injury benefits.
explain.spoken: When someone's off sick in France, the state fund pays part of their income, and it needs us to tell it what they've been earning. That's the salary certificate.

def: The schedule of each month's payroll deadlines: input cut-off, checks, approval, pay date and filings.

formal.ex: The [[payroll calendar]] for the coming year shall be agreed with the provider by 30 November.
formal.ex_us: The [[payroll calendar]] for the coming year shall be agreed upon with the vendor by November 30.

everyday.ex: Can you send the managers the [[payroll timetable]] so they stop sending overtime on the 28th?
everyday.ex_us: Can you send the managers the [[payroll schedule]] so they stop sending overtime on the 28th?

collocations: to work back from the pay date
note_fr: « To agree something » (UK) / « to agree on something » (US). « Calendar » désigne aussi l'agenda : « my calendar is full » ; le britannique dit aussi « diary » dans ce sens.

def: The monthly data that changes from one payroll to the next - overtime, absences, bonuses, starters and leavers - and must reach payroll before the cut-off.

formal.ex: Managers shall validate the [[variable payroll data]] for their teams in the HRIS by the 15th of each month.

everyday.ex: Half the [[payroll inputs]] still arrive by email, which is where the errors creep in.

note_fr: « Variable elements » est un calque peu clair : « inputs » est le terme du métier. Ne confondez pas avec « variable pay » (rémunération variable).

fr: date de clôture (de la paie, des éléments variables)
def: The last date on which changes can be taken into account in the current month's payroll.

formal.ex: Changes received after the [[cut-off date]] shall be processed in the following month's payroll.
formal.ex_us: Changes received after the [[cutoff date]] shall be processed in the following month's payroll.

everyday.ex: Sorry, we've missed the [[cut-off]] - it'll go through next month.
everyday.ex_us: Sorry, we missed the [[cutoff]] - it'll go through next month.

note_fr: Les Britanniques écrivent « cut-off » avec un trait d'union, les Américains souvent « cutoff » en un mot. Le verbe s'écrit toujours en deux mots : « to cut off ».

def: The formal approval of the month's payroll by an authorised person before salaries are paid.

formal.ex: [[Payroll approval]] shall be given by the HR Director or, in her absence, by the Finance Director.

everyday.ex: I can't give [[payroll sign-off]] until the reconciliation's done.

collocations: to sign off the payroll (UK) / to sign off on the payroll (US)
note_fr: « Validate » est un faux ami fréquent : en anglais, on « validates » des données (on vérifie qu'elles sont correctes) ; on « approves » ou on « signs off » une paie.

def: A difference between two figures or records that ought to match.

formal.ex: Any [[discrepancy]] above the agreed threshold shall be investigated and documented before payroll approval.

everyday.ex: There's a [[mismatch]] between the headcount in the HRIS and the number of payslips.
everyday.ex_us: There's a [[mismatch]] between the headcount in the HRIS and the number of pay stubs.

note_fr: « Gap » se dit d'un écart structurel (« pay gap ») ; pour un écart de rapprochement, dites « discrepancy », et « variance » pour un écart par rapport au budget ou au mois précédent.

fr: rapprochement (de la paie avec la comptabilité, la banque, les déclarations)
def: The check that payroll totals agree with other sources - the accounts, bank payments and social declarations - and that any difference is explained.

formal.ex: A [[payroll reconciliation]] between the payroll journal, the general ledger and the DSN shall be performed every month.

everyday.ex: We [[reconcile]] the payroll with the bank file before anything is paid out.

collocations: to reconcile payroll to the general ledger
note_fr: « Rapprochement » ne se traduit pas par « rapprochement » (réconciliation diplomatique). « To tie out » est le jargon des comptables américains pour « faire concorder ».

def: A quick overall check that figures look plausible, before going into detail.

formal.ex: A [[reasonableness check]] of gross pay against the previous month shall be performed for each cost centre.
formal.ex_us: A [[reasonableness check]] of gross pay against the previous month shall be performed for each cost center.

everyday.ex: Could you give these figures a quick [[sense check]] before they go to the CFO?
everyday.ex_us: Could you give these numbers a quick [[sanity check]] before they go to the CFO?

note_fr: « Coherence check » n'est pas idiomatique. « Sanity check » est très courant aux États-Unis ; certains Britanniques lui préfèrent « sense check », jugé plus neutre.

def: A check made on a few items chosen at random rather than on everything.

formal.ex: A [[sample check]] of twenty payslips shall be carried out each month by a person independent of their preparation.
formal.ex_us: [[Sample testing]] of twenty pay statements shall be performed each month by a person independent of their preparation.

everyday.ex: We do a [[spot check]] on a handful of payslips every month.
everyday.ex_us: We do a [[spot check]] on a handful of pay stubs every month.

note_fr: Le « sondage » statistique se dit « sampling » ; un sondage d'opinion est un « poll » ou une « survey ».

fr: principe des quatre yeux / double contrôle
def: The rule that a sensitive operation must be checked or approved by a second person before it takes effect.

formal.ex: Changes to employees' bank details are subject to the [[four-eyes principle]].
formal.ex_us: Changes to employees' bank details are subject to [[dual control]].

everyday.ex: Nothing goes to the bank without a [[second pair of eyes]] on it.
everyday.ex_us: Nothing goes to the bank without a [[second set of eyes]] on it.

note_fr: « Four-eyes » vient du vocabulaire bancaire européen ; aux États-Unis, on dit plutôt « dual control » ou « maker-checker ».

def: The control principle that no single person should be able to run a sensitive process from start to finish, for example both changing pay data and releasing payments.

formal.ex: The audit identified a lack of [[segregation of duties]]: the same user could create an employee and release payments.

everyday.ex: With only two people in payroll, it's hard to [[split the roles]] properly.

note_fr: « Separation of tasks » se comprend, mais « segregation of duties » (souvent abrégé « SoD ») est le terme consacré en audit. « Segregation » n'a ici aucune connotation raciale.

def: A record showing who changed what in a system, when, and with whose approval.

formal.ex: The system shall maintain a complete [[audit trail]] of all changes to salary data.

everyday.ex: Changing it straight in the database won't [[leave a trail]] - and that's exactly what auditors hate.

note_fr: « Traceability » existe (surtout dans l'industrie) ; pour les systèmes et la paie, « audit trail » est l'usage. Une trace écrite au sens large : « paper trail ».

fr: paie à blanc / paie en parallèle (lors d'un changement de système)
def: Running payroll in both the old and the new system for one or more months and comparing the results before switching over.

formal.ex: Two [[parallel runs]] shall be completed with no unexplained differences before the new payroll goes live.

everyday.ex: Let's do a [[dry run]] in September so we're not finding errors in October's real payroll.

collocations: to compare results line by line
note_fr: « White payroll » (calque de « paie à blanc ») n'existe pas. « Dry run » (répétition générale) s'emploie aussi hors de la paie.

def: A control that on its own is enough to prevent or detect a significant error in a process, and which auditors therefore test as a priority.

formal.ex: The monthly review of payroll variances has been designated as a [[key control]] and will be tested every quarter.

everyday.ex: Honestly, the bank-file review is [[the main safeguard]] - everything else is belt and braces.
everyday.ex_us: Honestly, the bank-file review is [[the main safeguard]] - everything else is belt and suspenders.

note_fr: « Preventive control » (qui empêche l'erreur) ≠ « detective control » (qui la détecte après coup). « Belt and braces » (UK) / « belt and suspenders » (US) : précaution redondante.

def: The liability recorded in the accounts for paid leave that employees have earned but not yet taken.

formal.ex: The [[accrued holiday pay]] shall be recalculated at each month end on the basis of leave balances in the HRIS.
formal.ex_us: The [[accrued vacation liability]] shall be recalculated at each month end on the basis of leave balances in the HRIS.

everyday.ex: The [[holiday accrual]] jumped in May because nobody took leave during the project.
everyday.ex_us: The [[PTO accrual]] jumped in May because nobody took time off during the project.

note_fr: En anglais comptable, « provision » désigne un passif incertain ; une charge à payer certaine est un « accrual ». Les congés payés français étant plus nombreux, ce poste surprend souvent les contrôleurs de gestion étrangers.

def: An external company that processes payroll on behalf of an employer.

formal.ex: The [[payroll service provider]] shall act only on the documented instructions of the Company.

everyday.ex: Our [[payroll provider]] has changed account managers three times this year.
everyday.ex_us: Our [[payroll vendor]] has changed account managers three times this year.

note_fr: « Prestataire » n'a pas d'équivalent unique : « provider », « supplier », « vendor » (US). « Prestator » n'existe pas.

def: The person who prepares, checks and processes the payroll and answers employees' pay questions.

formal.ex: The [[payroll administrator]] shall not hold access rights to approve payments.
formal.ex_us: The [[payroll specialist]] shall not hold access rights to approve payments.

everyday.ex: Ask [[payroll]] - they'll know why your overtime isn't on there.

note_fr: « Manager » implique l'encadrement d'une équipe : un gestionnaire de paie n'est pas un « payroll manager ». « Payroll clerk » est plus modeste et un peu daté.

fr: contrat de niveau de service / engagements de service
def: The part of an outsourcing contract that sets measurable service standards - deadlines, accuracy rates, response times - and what happens if they are missed.

formal.ex: Under the [[service level agreement]], the provider must deliver draft payslips no later than five working days before the pay date.
formal.ex_us: Under the [[service level agreement]], the vendor must deliver draft pay statements no later than five business days before the pay date.

everyday.ex: They've missed the [[SLA]] three months running - it's time to talk about service credits.
everyday.ex_us: They've missed the [[SLA]] three months in a row - it's time to talk about service credits.

note_fr: « SLA » se prononce lettre par lettre. Les « service credits » sont des remises dues par le prestataire en cas de non-respect ; le mot « penalties » est évité dans les contrats de droit anglais.

def: The provider's contractual obligation to help hand the service back to the client, or over to a new provider, at the end of the contract, including the transfer of data.

formal.ex: The [[exit management provisions]] require the provider to return the full payroll history in a usable format.
formal.ex_us: The [[transition assistance provisions]] require the vendor to return the full payroll history in a usable format.

everyday.ex: Before we sign with anyone, I want a proper [[exit plan]] - we can't be held hostage by a provider.
everyday.ex_us: Before we sign with anyone, I want a real [[exit plan]] - we can't be held hostage by a vendor.

collocations: to hand over to a new provider
note_fr: « Reversibility » est un calque peu compris hors des contrats rédigés par des Français. Parlez d'« exit assistance » ou d'« exit plan ».

fr: charges sociales (vues comme coût s'ajoutant au salaire)
def: The costs an employer pays on top of gross salary - mainly social security contributions - often expressed as a percentage of pay.

formal.ex: In France, [[employer on-costs]] represent a considerably higher share of gross salary than in the United States.
formal.ex_us: In France, the [[labor burden]] represents a considerably higher share of gross salary than in the United States.

everyday.ex: Don't forget the [[on-costs]] - a fifty-thousand salary costs us a lot more than fifty.
everyday.ex_us: Don't forget the [[burden]] - a fifty-thousand salary costs us a lot more than fifty.

note_fr: « Social charges » se comprend mais sonne français : dites « employer contributions » pour l'aspect juridique, « on-costs » (UK) ou « burden » (US) pour parler de coût.

def: The total cost of running payroll divided by the number of payslips produced, used to benchmark providers or countries.

formal.ex: The [[cost per payslip]] in France remains above the group average, owing chiefly to the complexity of local rules.
formal.ex_us: The [[cost per pay statement]] in France remains above the corporate average, due mainly to the complexity of local rules.

everyday.ex: On a [[cost per head]] basis French payroll looks expensive, but it isn't a like-for-like comparison.
everyday.ex_us: On a [[cost per employee]] basis French payroll looks expensive, but it isn't an apples-to-apples comparison.

note_fr: « Bulletin » ne s'emploie pas pour une fiche de paie : « payslip » (UK), « pay stub » ou « pay statement » (US). « Like for like » (UK) = « apples to apples » (US).

def: The ongoing tracking of changes in laws, rates and administrative rules that affect HR and payroll.

formal.ex: The provider is responsible for [[regulatory monitoring]] and for updating contribution rates in the payroll engine.

everyday.ex: With rates changing every January, it's a full-time job to [[keep on top of]] French payroll rules.

collocations: to keep abreast of legal changes
note_fr: « Watch » (calque de « veille ») n'a pas ce sens en anglais. « Horizon scanning » est apprécié dans les organisations britanniques pour l'anticipation des évolutions.

def: The amount of pay - salary plus bonuses and taxable benefits - on which social security contributions are calculated.

formal.ex: Benefits in kind form part of the [[earnings subject to contributions]].
formal.ex_us: Fringe benefits form part of the [[wages subject to payroll taxes]].

everyday.ex: The auditor's point is that the car allowance should have been in the [[contribution base]].
everyday.ex_us: The auditor's point is that the car allowance should have been included in the [[wage base]].

collocations: to be included in the contribution base
to be excluded from the base
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « wage base » désigne aussi le plafond au-delà duquel certaines taxes ne sont plus dues (« Social Security wage base »). L'assiette est au cœur de nombreux redressements URSSAF.

fr: allègements / réduction générale des cotisations patronales
def: A statutory reduction in the social security contributions an employer pays - in France mainly on lower salaries - which payroll must calculate correctly.

formal.ex: The company qualifies for the general [[reduction in employer contributions]] on salaries below the statutory threshold.

everyday.ex: If the hours are wrong in the system, the [[contribution relief]] is wrong too - and that's exactly what URSSAF picks up.
everyday.ex_us: If the hours are wrong in the system, the [[payroll tax relief]] is wrong too - and that's exactly what URSSAF picks up.

collocations: to lose the benefit of a reduction
note_fr: « Exoneration » signifie en anglais « disculpation » (innocenter quelqu'un) : pour une exonération de cotisations, dites « exemption » ou « relief ». Les paramètres de calcul changent souvent : vérifiez-les chaque année.

def: The single electronic return, generated from payroll, that every French employer files each month to report each employee's pay, contributions and employment events to the social security bodies and the tax authorities.

formal.ex: The [[monthly social declaration]] must be filed by the 5th or the 15th of the following month, depending on headcount and pay date.

everyday.ex: Payroll's done, but [[the DSN]] still has to go out by the fifth.

note_fr: Comparable aux « Real Time Information (RTI) submissions » britanniques transmises au fisc à chaque paie ; aux États-Unis, l'équivalent est éclaté (déclarations trimestrielles à l'IRS, déclarations des États, formulaires W-2 annuels).

explain.written: The DSN (déclaration sociale nominative) is a monthly electronic filing, generated from payroll, through which French employers report each employee's pay, contributions, withholding tax and employment events to all the social security and tax bodies at once.
explain.spoken: The DSN is one big monthly file that comes straight out of payroll and tells the authorities who we paid, how much, and what we owe. It replaced dozens of separate forms.

def: To submit an official declaration of figures, such as pay or contributions, to the authorities.

formal.ex: The employer shall [[submit a return]] for each establishment by the due date.
formal.ex_us: The employer shall [[submit a filing]] for each establishment by the due date.

everyday.ex: We [[filed]] on time, but the system rejected two records.

note_fr: « To declare » s'emploie pour un revenu (« to declare income ») ; pour le dépôt d'un formulaire, on dit « to file » ou « to submit ». Une déclaration se dit « return » (UK) ou « filing » (US).

fr: date limite de dépôt / échéance déclarative
def: The last date by which a return or declaration must reach the authorities.

formal.ex: Failure to meet the [[due date for filing]] gives rise to a late-filing penalty.
formal.ex_us: Failure to meet the [[filing due date]] results in a late-filing penalty.

everyday.ex: We can't move the [[filing deadline]] - it's set by law, not by the provider.
everyday.ex_us: We can't move the [[filing deadline]] - it's set by law, not by the vendor.

note_fr: « Deadline » est un nom ; « échoir » se dit « to fall due ». Plutôt que « the deadline expires », on dit naturellement « the deadline passes ».

fr: déclaration rectificative / correction d'une période antérieure
def: A new declaration, or a correction in a later one, filed to put right errors in a return already submitted.

formal.ex: Errors identified after submission shall be corrected by a [[corrective return]] or in the following month's declaration.
formal.ex_us: Errors identified after submission shall be corrected by a [[corrected filing]] or in the following month's declaration.

everyday.ex: We'll have to put in an [[amended return]] for March - the bonus was reported twice.
everyday.ex_us: We'll have to submit an [[amended filing]] for March - the bonus was reported twice.

note_fr: « Rectificative » n'a pas d'équivalent direct (« rectified » est rare). En DSN, la plupart des erreurs se régularisent dans la déclaration du mois suivant plutôt que par une déclaration « annule et remplace ».

fr: signalement d'événement (DSN : arrêt de travail, reprise, fin de contrat)
def: A separate DSN filing that the employer must send shortly after a specific event, such as sick leave, a return to work or the end of a contract.

formal.ex: An [[event-based report]] must be filed promptly when a contract ends, so that the employee's unemployment rights can be assessed.

everyday.ex: Did anyone send the [[event report]] for Marc's sick leave? The fund's chasing us.

note_fr: « Signalement » se traduit ici par « report » ou « notification », pas par « signal ». Ces signalements ont leurs propres délais, courts et distincts de l'échéance mensuelle.

explain.written: In addition to the monthly DSN, French employers must file DSN event reports when certain events occur - mainly sick leave, a return to work and the end of a contract - so that social security benefits can be calculated without delay.
explain.spoken: On top of the monthly file, there are one-off DSN reports for specific events - someone goes off sick, comes back, or leaves - and they have their own short deadlines.

def: An additional amount charged by the collection body when contributions are paid or declared late.

formal.ex: A [[surcharge for late payment]] is applied automatically to contributions not paid by the due date.
formal.ex_us: A [[penalty for late payment]] is applied automatically to contributions not paid by the due date.

everyday.ex: It's only a day late, but there'll still be a [[late-payment penalty]].
everyday.ex_us: It's only a day late, but there'll still be a [[late fee]].

collocations: to apply for remission of surcharges
note_fr: « Majoration » se traduit selon le contexte : « surcharge » ou « penalty » pour un retard, « premium » pour des heures supplémentaires. Le mot « majoration » n'existe pas en anglais.

term.uk: the URSSAF (social security contributions collection body)
term.us: the URSSAF (social security contributions collection body)

def: The French body that collects social security contributions from employers and checks, through audits, that they have been correctly calculated and paid.

formal.ex: Contributions are paid monthly to the [[social security collection agency]] on the basis of the DSN.

everyday.ex: [[URSSAF]] has written to say they're coming in March.

collocations: to be up to date with URSSAF
note_fr: Les anglophones disent « URSSAF » ou « the URSSAF » ; ajoutez une glose la première fois. Équivalents approximatifs : HMRC, qui collecte aussi les « National Insurance contributions », au Royaume-Uni ; l'IRS et les agences des États aux États-Unis.

explain.written: URSSAF is the French network of bodies that collects social security contributions from employers and the self-employed and audits them to check that contributions have been correctly calculated and paid.
explain.spoken: URSSAF is basically the agency we pay our social charges to - and the one that comes and audits us to check we've paid the right amount.

def: An inspection of an employer's payroll records by the collection body to check that contributions have been correctly calculated and paid.

formal.ex: The company is currently undergoing a [[social security audit]] covering the last three years.
formal.ex_us: The company is currently undergoing a [[payroll tax audit]] covering the last three years.

everyday.ex: We had an [[URSSAF audit]] last year and the company cars cost us a fortune.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, on parlerait d'un « HMRC employer compliance review » ; aux États-Unis, d'un « employment tax audit » de l'IRS ou d'un État. « Control » ne s'emploie pas dans ce sens : dites « audit » ou « inspection ».

def: The letter by which the collection body informs an employer in advance that an audit will take place, and when.

formal.ex: The [[notice of audit]] specifies the start date and the documents to be made available to the inspector.

everyday.ex: The [[audit letter]] came in yesterday - they want to start on the 12th.

collocations: to receive a notice of audit
the charter of the audited employer
note_fr: L'avis renvoie à la charte du cotisant contrôlé, qui rappelle les droits de l'employeur. « Avis » se traduit ici par « notice », jamais par « advice » (conseil).

def: The span of past months or years that an audit can cover, limited by the statute of limitations.

formal.ex: The [[period under review]] covers the three calendar years preceding the audit and the current year.
formal.ex_us: The [[audit period]] covers the three calendar years preceding the audit and the current year.

everyday.ex: In cases of undeclared work, the [[look-back period]] is longer.

note_fr: « Prescription » se dit « limitation period » (UK) ou « statute of limitations » (US), jamais « prescription » (ordonnance médicale). En cas de travail dissimulé, la période contrôlable est allongée.

def: The letter sent at the end of a French social security audit, setting out each finding, its legal basis and the amounts to be reassessed, and opening a period for the employer to respond.

formal.ex: The employer has a limited period from receipt of the [[letter of observations]] in which to submit its response.
formal.ex_us: The employer has a limited period from receipt of the [[letter of findings]] in which to submit its response.

everyday.ex: The [[findings letter]] lists six points - and four of them are about benefits in kind.

collocations: to respond to the letter of observations
note_fr: Le délai de réponse est en principe de 30 jours, prolongeable sur demande : vérifiez toujours ce qu'indique la lettre. « Observations » est faible en anglais ; parlez de « findings » à vos interlocuteurs.

explain.written: The lettre d'observations is the formal letter that closes the inspection phase of an URSSAF audit: it lists each finding, its legal basis and the proposed reassessment, and gives the employer a set period to respond before any demand for payment is issued.
explain.spoken: It's the inspector's written findings at the end of the audit. We get a few weeks to push back on each point before they send us the bill.

def: The additional contributions claimed by the collection body after an audit, on top of what the employer originally paid.

formal.ex: The audit resulted in a [[reassessment of contributions]] of 84,000 euros, plus late-payment surcharges.
formal.ex_us: The audit resulted in an [[assessment of additional taxes]] of 84,000 euros, plus late-payment penalties.

everyday.ex: Most of the [[reassessment]] comes down to one thing: the company cars.
everyday.ex_us: Most of the [[adjustment]] comes down to one thing: the company cars.

collocations: a reassessment in the employer's favour
note_fr: Ne traduisez pas par « recovery » ni « straightening ». « Redressement judiciaire » est tout autre chose : « administration » (UK) / « court-supervised reorganization » (US). Un contrôle peut aussi aboutir à un remboursement en faveur de l'employeur.

def: The official demand, sent after an audit or a missed payment, requiring the employer to pay within a set time, failing which enforcement can begin.

formal.ex: A [[formal notice to pay]] was served on the company once its response to the findings had been considered.
formal.ex_us: A [[formal demand for payment]] was issued to the company once its response to the findings had been considered.

everyday.ex: We've had the [[final demand]], so if we want to contest it, the clock is ticking.
everyday.ex_us: We got the [[final notice]], so if we want to contest it, the clock is ticking.

collocations: to challenge within the time limit
note_fr: « Put in default » est un calque fréquent et peu idiomatique. La mise en demeure fait courir le délai de contestation : notez précisément sa date de réception.

fr: contester un redressement (saisir la commission de recours amiable)
def: To dispute the amounts claimed after an audit, first before a review board within the collection body and then, if necessary, in court.

formal.ex: The company intends to [[contest the reassessment]] before the amicable appeals board within the statutory time limit.
formal.ex_us: The company intends to [[appeal the assessment]] before the internal appeals board within the statutory time limit.

everyday.ex: Two of the points are worth [[challenging]]; the rest, frankly, we should just pay.
everyday.ex_us: Two of the points are worth [[fighting]]; the rest, frankly, we should just pay.

collocations: to take the matter to court
note_fr: Le recours devant la commission de recours amiable (CRA) est un préalable obligatoire avant le tribunal. « Amicable » doit être glosé : « an internal review board of the collection body ».

def: An agreement allowing an employer to pay a debt to the authorities in several instalments over an agreed period.

formal.ex: The company has requested a [[payment schedule]] over twelve months for the reassessed contributions.
formal.ex_us: The company has requested an [[installment plan]] over twelve months for the reassessed contributions.

everyday.ex: If cash is tight, we can ask for a [[time-to-pay arrangement]] - they're usually open to it.
everyday.ex_us: If cash is tight, we can ask for an [[installment agreement]] - they're usually open to it.

collocations: to keep up with the payments
note_fr: Orthographe : « instalment » (UK), « installment » (US). « Time to Pay arrangement » est le terme officiel du fisc britannique (HMRC) ; « installment agreement » celui de l'IRS américain.

def: The cancellation or reduction, on request, of surcharges for late payment, usually granted where the employer has acted in good faith.

formal.ex: Once the contributions have been settled, the company may apply for [[remission of surcharges]].
formal.ex_us: Once the contributions have been paid, the company may request [[penalty abatement]].

everyday.ex: If we pay the contributions now, they may agree to [[waive the penalties]].

note_fr: « Remise » n'est pas ici une remise commerciale (« discount »). La remise des majorations suppose en principe le paiement préalable des cotisations dues.

def: A formal written answer from the authorities, requested by the employer, on how a rule applies to its specific situation, by which the authorities are then bound.

formal.ex: Before rolling out the new allowance, the company sought an [[advance ruling]] on its treatment for contribution purposes.

everyday.ex: If we're not sure the scheme is exempt, why not [[get a ruling]] first?

collocations: to be bound by a ruling
note_fr: Le rescrit n'engage l'administration que pour la situation décrite et tant que les faits et le droit ne changent pas. Équivalents : « private letter ruling » de l'IRS (US), « non-statutory clearance » de HMRC (UK).

fr: contrôle sur pièces (sans visite sur place)
def: An audit carried out remotely, from documents sent in by the employer, without inspectors visiting the premises.

formal.ex: Smaller employers may be subject to a [[desk-based audit]] conducted entirely on the basis of the documents they submit.
formal.ex_us: Smaller employers may be subject to a [[desk audit]] conducted entirely on the basis of the documents they submit.

everyday.ex: It's only a [[remote audit]], but they still want three years of payroll journals.

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, l'IRS distingue « correspondence audit » (par courrier), « office audit » et « field audit » (sur place). Ne traduisez jamais « sur pièces » par « on pieces ».

fr: procès-verbal (de l'inspection du travail) / dresser procès-verbal
def: A formal written record in which a labour inspector records an offence; it is sent to the public prosecutor and can lead to criminal proceedings.

formal.ex: The inspector may draw up an [[official report]] recording the offence and forward it to the public prosecutor.
formal.ex_us: The inspector may draw up an [[official report]] recording the offense and forward it to the public prosecutor.

everyday.ex: If they find people working without a contract, we'll [[be written up]] - and that goes straight to the prosecutor.

collocations: to refer a case to the public prosecutor
note_fr: Ne confondez pas avec le procès-verbal de réunion (« minutes ») et ne traduisez jamais par « verbal process ». L'inspecteur peut aussi se contenter d'observations écrites ou d'une mise en demeure.

explain.written: A procès-verbal is a formal report in which a French labour inspector records an offence; it is forwarded to the public prosecutor, who decides whether to bring criminal proceedings.
explain.spoken: It's the inspector's official write-up of an offence. It goes to the prosecutor, so it's a real step up from a warning letter.

def: A financial penalty imposed directly by an administrative authority, without going to court.

formal.ex: Failure to keep working-time records may give rise to an [[administrative fine]] for each employee concerned.

everyday.ex: We could [[be fined]] for every employee whose hours weren't recorded.

note_fr: En France, l'administration du travail peut infliger des amendes administratives dans certains domaines, sans passer par un juge. « Amende » n'a rien à voir avec « to amend » (modifier).

def: The legal duties to send information - declarations, indicators, reports - to the authorities, or to publish it, by set dates.

formal.ex: The subsidiary's [[reporting obligations]] are summarised in the attached compliance calendar.
formal.ex_us: The subsidiary's [[reporting requirements]] are summarized in the attached compliance calendar.

everyday.ex: January is a nightmare - all the annual [[filings]] land at once.

note_fr: « Declarative obligations » est un calque. En anglais, « reporting » couvre à la fois les déclarations aux autorités et le reporting interne.

def: A French statutory report, required in companies with at least 300 employees, that sets out key workforce figures - headcount, pay, working conditions, training, industrial relations - over three years.

formal.ex: The [[annual social report]] is submitted to the works council for its opinion and sent to the labour inspector.

everyday.ex: Can we reuse the [[workforce report]] figures for the group's ESG survey?

collocations: to prepare the annual social report
note_fr: « Social balance sheet », traduction littérale, est incompréhensible. « Social » renvoie en anglais à la société au sens large : précisez « workforce » ou « employment ».

explain.written: The bilan social is an annual report that French companies with 300 or more employees must draw up, presenting key workforce indicators over a three-year period, for submission to the works council.
explain.spoken: It's an annual pack of workforce statistics - headcount, pay, absence, training - that larger French companies have to produce for the works council.

fr: DOETH (déclaration obligatoire d'emploi des travailleurs handicapés)
def: The annual declaration, now made through the DSN, by which French employers report how many disabled workers they employ against the legal quota and calculate any contribution due.

formal.ex: The [[annual disability employment return]] is now filed through the DSN, and any contribution due is paid to URSSAF.
formal.ex_us: The [[annual disability employment report]] is now filed through the DSN, and any contribution due is paid to URSSAF.

everyday.ex: The [[disability return]] shows we're short of the quota again, so there'll be a contribution to pay.
everyday.ex_us: The [[disability report]] shows we're short of the quota again, so there'll be a contribution to pay.

collocations: the employment quota for disabled workers
note_fr: Le Royaume-Uni n'a pas de quota et les États-Unis ne fixent des objectifs qu'aux entreprises sous contrat fédéral : la notion doit être expliquée. Écrivez « disabled workers » ou « workers with disabilities », jamais « handicapped ».

explain.written: The DOETH is the annual declaration, made through the DSN, by which French employers with 20 or more employees report their employment of disabled workers against the statutory quota and pay a contribution if they fall short.
explain.spoken: Every year we have to declare how many people with a recognised disability we employ. If we're below the quota, we pay a contribution.

def: Work hidden, in whole or in part, from the authorities - for example an unregistered business, an undeclared employee or under-reported hours.

formal.ex: The client company may be held jointly liable where its subcontractor has engaged in [[undeclared work]].
formal.ex_us: The client company may be held jointly liable where its subcontractor has engaged in [[unreported employment]].

everyday.ex: The inspectors found two drivers being paid [[off the books]].

informal.ex: He was doing weekend shifts for them, paid [[cash in hand]].
informal.ex_us: He was doing weekend shifts for them, paid [[under the table]].

collocations: to be paid off the books
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « illegal working » désigne surtout l'emploi de personnes sans droit au travail (immigration) : ne l'employez pas pour « travail dissimulé ». La notion française est large et inclut la sous-déclaration d'heures.

def: The form of undeclared work in which an employer deliberately fails to declare an employee or issue payslips, or shows fewer hours on the payslip than were actually worked.

formal.ex: Recording fewer hours on the payslip than were actually worked may constitute [[concealed employment]].
formal.ex_us: Recording fewer hours on the pay statement than were actually worked may constitute [[concealed employment]].

everyday.ex: Paying overtime as 'expenses' is [[under-declaring hours]], and the inspectors know that trick.
everyday.ex_us: Paying overtime as 'expenses' is [[underreporting hours]], and the inspectors know that trick.

collocations: to fail to issue a payslip
note_fr: L'élément intentionnel est requis : une simple erreur de paie n'est pas du travail dissimulé. Les conséquences sont lourdes : sanctions pénales, annulation des allègements de cotisations, solidarité financière du donneur d'ordre.

explain.written: Dissimulation d'emploi salarié is the form of undeclared work in which an employer intentionally fails to make the pre-hiring declaration or to issue payslips, or shows fewer hours on payslips than were actually worked.
explain.spoken: It's when an employer deliberately hides an employee, or part of their hours, from the authorities - no declaration, no payslip, or a payslip showing fewer hours than they really worked.

def: A company that employs temporary workers and places them with client businesses for limited assignments.

formal.ex: The [[employment business]] remains the legal employer of the agency worker throughout the assignment.
formal.ex_us: The [[temporary staffing firm]] remains the legal employer of the temporary worker throughout the assignment.

everyday.ex: We've asked the [[temp agency]] for three more people for the Christmas peak.
everyday.ex_us: We've asked the [[staffing agency]] for three more people for the holiday peak.

note_fr: En droit britannique, l'« employment business » (qui place des intérimaires) se distingue de l'« employment agency » (cabinet de recrutement). « Interim » désigne en anglais un intérim de direction (« interim manager »), pas l'intérim au sens français.

def: The business in which an agency worker actually carries out the work, as opposed to the agency that employs him or her.

formal.ex: The [[hirer]] is responsible for health and safety and working time at the place of work.
formal.ex_us: The [[client company]] is responsible for health and safety and working time at the worksite.

everyday.ex: The agency pays them, but the [[end client]] decides their hours.
everyday.ex_us: The agency pays them, but the [[client]] decides their hours.

note_fr: « User company » (calque) se comprend dans les textes européens (« user undertaking »), mais « hirer » est le terme du droit britannique. En France, l'entreprise utilisatrice répond des conditions de travail (durée du travail, sécurité) pendant la mission.

fr: cas de recours au travail temporaire

term.uk: permitted grounds for using agency staff
term.us: permitted grounds for using temporary staff

def: The limited list of situations in which French law allows a business to use temporary agency workers, such as replacing an absent employee or coping with a temporary increase in activity.

formal.ex: Each assignment contract must state one of the [[permitted grounds]] for agency work set out in the Labour Code.
formal.ex_us: Each assignment contract must state one of the [[permitted grounds]] for temporary work set out in the Labor Code.

everyday.ex: You can't bring in temps to fill a permanent job - each assignment needs [[a legitimate reason]], like covering an absence.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, le recours à l'intérim est libre : vos interlocuteurs ignorent souvent que la France l'encadre strictement. Un recours irrégulier expose à la requalification de la mission en CDI auprès de l'entreprise utilisatrice.

explain.written: French law allows businesses to use temporary agency workers only for specific, temporary tasks listed in the Labour Code - for example replacing an absent employee or coping with a temporary increase in activity - and never to fill a permanent position or to replace striking employees.
explain.spoken: In France you can't use temps whenever you like. There has to be one of the reasons the law allows - covering an absence, a temporary peak - and you can never use them for a permanent job or to replace strikers.

def: The for-profit supply of staff to another business outside the regulated temporary agency framework, or any for-profit supply of labour that harms the workers or circumvents the law, both prohibited in France.

formal.ex: A contract that merely provides workers, with no specific service or know-how, may be treated as an [[unlawful supply of labour]].
formal.ex_us: A contract that merely provides workers, with no specific service or know-how, may be treated as an [[unlawful supply of labor]].

everyday.ex: If the 'consultants' just sit in our teams taking orders from our managers, it looks like [[labour-only subcontracting]].
everyday.ex_us: If the 'consultants' just sit in our teams taking orders from our managers, it looks like [[labor-only contracting]].

collocations: to take orders from the client's managers
note_fr: Notion largement inconnue au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, où la mise à disposition de personnel est courante. Un indice clé : qui donne les ordres au quotidien ? Si c'est le client, le contrat de prestation est fragile.

explain.written: French law prohibits the for-profit supply of staff outside the regulated temporary agency framework (prêt de main-d'œuvre illicite) and any for-profit supply of labour that harms the workers or circumvents the law (marchandage); genuine subcontracting must involve a specific service delivered with the contractor's own know-how and management.
explain.spoken: In France, a contractor can't just rent people out to you for profit unless it's a temp agency. If their staff work under your managers like your own employees, it can be treated as an illegal supply of labour.

def: An outside business that carries out part of the work, or a service, for a company under a commercial contract.

formal.ex: The Company shall verify that each [[contractor]] is duly registered and up to date with its social security obligations.

everyday.ex: The cleaning is done by a [[subcontractor]], so we need their URSSAF certificate every six months.

note_fr: Le « sous-traitant » au sens du RGPD est un « data processor » : rien à voir. En anglais, « contractor » désigne le prestataire principal et « subcontractor » celui à qui il confie une partie du travail ; dans la pratique, les deux s'emploient souvent indifféremment.

def: The French client company's legal obligation to check, at signature and periodically during any contract above a set value, that its contractor is registered and up to date with its social security declarations and payments.

formal.ex: Under its [[due diligence obligation]], the client must obtain the contractor's certificate of compliance when the contract is signed and every six months thereafter.

everyday.ex: Procurement thought the [[contractor checks]] were HR's job, and HR thought they were procurement's.
everyday.ex_us: Procurement thought the [[vendor checks]] were HR's job, and HR thought they were procurement's.

collocations: to obtain documents from the contractor
note_fr: Ne confondez pas avec le « devoir de vigilance » des grandes sociétés (loi de 2017 sur les droits humains et l'environnement dans la chaîne d'approvisionnement). Il s'agit ici de lutter contre le travail dissimulé.

explain.written: The obligation de vigilance requires a French company that contracts for services above a set value to check, at signature and every six months, that its contractor is registered and has filed and paid its social security contributions; if it fails to do so, it may be held jointly liable should the contractor use undeclared work.
explain.spoken: Whenever we use a contractor above a certain amount, we have to collect proof that they're properly registered and paying their social charges - at the start and every six months. If we don't, and they turn out to be using undeclared workers, we can end up paying for it.

def: A certificate issued by URSSAF confirming that a business is registered and up to date with its social security declarations and payments, which clients must obtain from their contractors.

formal.ex: The supplier shall provide an up-to-date [[certificate of compliance]] issued by URSSAF every six months for the duration of the contract.

everyday.ex: Their [[URSSAF certificate]] expired in March and nobody asked for a new one.

collocations: to check that a certificate is authentic
note_fr: Vérifiez l'authenticité de l'attestation (code de sécurité vérifiable sur le site de l'URSSAF) : une simple copie ne suffit pas. « Vigilance certificate » n'est pas compris sans explication.

explain.written: The attestation de vigilance is a certificate issued by URSSAF confirming that a business is registered and has filed and paid its social security contributions; a client company must obtain it from its contractors and check that it is authentic.
explain.spoken: It's a certificate from URSSAF saying the contractor is properly registered and up to date with its social charges. We have to collect it and check it's genuine.

def: A rule under which each of several parties can be made to pay the whole of a debt; in France, a client that failed to carry out its checks can be made to pay the taxes, contributions and wages owed by a contractor using undeclared work.

formal.ex: Failure to carry out the required checks exposes the client to [[joint and several liability]] for the contributions and penalties owed by the contractor.

everyday.ex: If the cleaning firm turns out to be using undeclared workers, we could end up [[footing the bill]] for their unpaid contributions.

collocations: to be held jointly and severally liable
note_fr: « Financial solidarity » est un contresens : il évoque l'entraide. « Joint and several liability » est le terme juridique exact pour la solidarité entre débiteurs.

def: The fact of following the laws, regulations and internal rules that apply to an organisation.

formal.ex: The HR Director is responsible for ensuring the subsidiary's [[compliance]] with French employment and social security law.

everyday.ex: Before we sign off the new policy, can Legal confirm we're [[compliant]]?

note_fr: « Conformity » s'emploie pour des produits ou des normes techniques ; pour le droit, on dit « compliance ». Construction : « compliance with », jamais « compliance to ».

def: A failure to follow a law, regulation or internal rule.

formal.ex: Any [[non-compliance]] identified during the review shall be reported to the Group Compliance Officer within five working days.
formal.ex_us: Any [[noncompliance]] identified during the review shall be reported to the Corporate Compliance Officer within five business days.

everyday.ex: It's not a disaster, but it's a [[compliance issue]] and it needs fixing before the inspector comes back.

note_fr: Américain : « noncompliance » en un mot ; britannique : avec trait d'union. « Manquement » se traduit aussi par « failure to » + verbe : « failure to keep records ».

def: To make the changes needed so that a practice, document or system meets legal requirements.

formal.ex: The registers were [[brought into compliance]] within the period set by the inspector.

everyday.uk: to get one's house in order
everyday.us: to get one's house in order
everyday.ex: Let's [[get our house in order]] before head office sends the auditors in.
everyday.ex_us: Let's [[get our house in order]] before corporate sends the auditors in.

collocations: to bring practices into line with the law
note_fr: « Régulariser » se traduit selon le cas par « to bring into compliance », « to rectify » ou « to put right » ; « to regularise » existe mais ne couvre pas tous ces sens.

fr: calendrier des obligations légales / échéancier de conformité
def: A schedule of every recurring legal deadline - filings, consultations, publications, registers - with the person responsible for each.

formal.ex: The HR [[compliance calendar]] is reviewed each December and shared with Group Legal.
formal.ex_us: The HR [[compliance calendar]] is reviewed each December and shared with Corporate Legal.

everyday.ex: Put the index publication on the [[deadlines tracker]] - we can't afford to miss it again.

collocations: to assign an owner to each deadline
note_fr: « Échéancier » n'a pas de traduction unique : « calendar », « schedule », « timeline », ou « payment schedule » pour des paiements échelonnés.

fr: manquer une échéance / dépasser la date limite
def: To fail to do something by the date on which it was due.

formal.uk: to fail to meet a deadline
formal.us: to fail to meet a deadline
formal.ex: Should the provider [[fail to meet a deadline]], it shall notify the Company immediately and propose remedial action.

everyday.ex: We've never [[missed a deadline]] on the DSN, and I'd like to keep it that way.

note_fr: Respecter un délai : « to meet a deadline », pas « to respect a deadline ». « Échéance » peut aussi se traduire par « due date » (date d'exigibilité d'un paiement).

def: To contact someone again to remind them to do something they have not yet done.

formal.ex: If the documents have not been received by Friday, HR will [[send a reminder]] to the managers concerned.

everyday.ex: Could you [[chase up]] the managers who haven't sent their overtime?
everyday.ex_us: Could you [[follow up]] with the managers who haven't sent their overtime?

informal.ex: I'll [[nudge]] Simon again - he's still sitting on the timesheets.
informal.ex_us: I'll [[ping]] Simon again - he's still sitting on the timesheets.

note_fr: « To relaunch » est un contresens (relancer un produit, une campagne). En britannique, « to chase » n'a rien d'agressif ; l'américain préfère « to follow up » ou « to circle back ».

def: A structured review of an organisation's HR practices, records and compliance with employment law, carried out internally or by an outside firm.

formal.ex: An external [[HR compliance audit]] will be conducted at each French site before the end of the financial year.
formal.ex_us: An external [[HR compliance audit]] will be conducted at each French site before the end of the fiscal year.

everyday.ex: The [[HR audit]] picked up our temp contracts - the reason for using a temp wasn't always written down.

note_fr: « Social audit » désigne souvent l'audit RSE des fournisseurs (conditions de travail dans la chaîne d'approvisionnement) : pour l'audit social au sens français, dites « HR audit » ou « employment law audit ». Exercice : « financial year » (UK), « fiscal year » (US).

def: The independent function within a group that reviews processes and controls and reports on risks to senior management and the audit committee.

formal.ex: The [[internal audit]] team will review the French payroll process as part of its annual plan.

everyday.ex: Make sure the evidence folders are complete - [[the auditors]] are in next week.

note_fr: Ne confondez pas « internal audit » (audit interne, fonction du groupe) et « internal control » (contrôle interne, ensemble des contrôles opérationnels).

def: The set of checks, approvals and rules built into a process to prevent or detect errors and fraud.

formal.ex: The payroll process falls within the group's [[internal control framework]] and is tested every year.

everyday.ex: The [[controls]] are fine on paper - the problem is that nobody keeps evidence they've been done.

note_fr: « Contrôle » se traduit selon le sens : « control » (mesure de maîtrise d'un risque), « check » (vérification), « audit » ou « inspection » (contrôle par une autorité). Un « contrôle URSSAF » n'est jamais « a control ».

fr: faiblesse majeure (déficience significative) du contrôle interne
def: A serious flaw in internal controls that creates a reasonable possibility that a material error will not be prevented or detected in time.

formal.ex: The absence of any review of changes to bank details was reported to the audit committee as a [[material weakness]].

everyday.ex: Nobody checks bank-detail changes? That's a [[major gap in the controls]].
everyday.ex_us: Nobody checks bank-detail changes? That's a [[major control gap]].

collocations: to report to the audit committee
note_fr: Terme précis du référentiel américain (loi Sarbanes-Oxley) : une filiale française d'un groupe coté aux États-Unis peut y être soumise. Le degré inférieur est la « significant deficiency ». « Material » signifie ici « significatif », pas « matériel ».

def: A periodic exercise in which local teams assess and certify, usually through a questionnaire, whether their own key controls are operating.

formal.ex: The French subsidiary completes a [[control self-assessment]] twice a year, signed off by the HR Director and the Finance Director.

everyday.ex: The [[self-certification]] is only worth something if we can show the evidence behind each 'yes'.

collocations: to certify that controls are operating
to be tested by internal audit
note_fr: « Auto-evaluation » n'existe pas : le préfixe anglais est « self- ». Ne répondez jamais « yes » sans preuve : l'audit interne vérifie souvent par sondage.

def: A step taken to fix a problem that has been identified and to stop it happening again.

formal.ex: Each finding shall be addressed by a [[corrective action]] with a named owner and a target date.

everyday.ex: The quick [[fix]] is to lock the field; the real answer is to retrain the team.

note_fr: « Corrective measure » se comprend, mais « corrective action » est l'usage dans les plans d'audit. « Action » est dénombrable : « three corrective actions ».

fr: plan de remédiation / plan d'actions correctives
def: A structured plan setting out how, by whom and by when each problem identified in an audit or inspection will be fixed.

formal.ex: A [[remediation plan]] addressing each of the auditors' findings shall be submitted within thirty days.

everyday.ex: Let's agree an [[action plan]] with dates before the auditors leave the building.
everyday.ex_us: Let's agree on an [[action plan]] with dates before the auditors leave the building.

collocations: to draw up a remediation plan
note_fr: « To remediate » appartient au jargon de l'audit et de la conformité ; « to remedy » est plus général (remédier à). À l'oral, « action plan » ou « fix » suffisent.

def: The named person accountable for completing a specific action in a plan by its due date.

formal.ex: Each [[action owner]] shall report progress monthly to the HR compliance committee.

everyday.ex: Who's going to [[own]] the register clean-up?

note_fr: Dans un plan d'action, « responsable » se traduit mieux par « owner » ou « accountable ». Dans une matrice RACI, « responsible » (qui exécute) ≠ « accountable » (qui répond du résultat).

def: To have an audit finding formally marked as resolved, usually after providing evidence that the corrective action has been completed.

formal.ex: Internal audit will only [[close the finding]] once evidence of three months' operation of the control has been provided.

everyday.ex: If we send the evidence this week, they can [[close out]] four of the six points.

note_fr: « To lift a recommendation » est un calque de « lever ». En anglais, une recommandation est « implemented » et la constatation (« finding ») est « closed ».

fr: prendre des raccourcis (au détriment des règles)
def: To do something in the quickest or cheapest way, skipping steps or checks that should be carried out.

formal.ex: Under no circumstances may staff [[circumvent procedures]] in order to meet a payroll deadline.

everyday.ex: We're short-staffed, but we can't [[cut corners]] on the bank-detail checks.

note_fr: « Shortcut » (raccourci) est neutre ; « to cut corners » est toujours péjoratif. Pour « s'arranger avec les règles », dites « to bend the rules ».
